articles.title: From curl to Python requests: A Flag-by-Flag Conversion Guide
articles.excerpt: Originally published on iLoveDevTool. Right-click a request in browser DevTools, choose "Copy as cURL", and you get a complete command: URL, headers, body, cookies — everything. The next step is usual…
articles.body: Originally published on iLoveDevTool . Why developers keep converting curl to Python Right-click a request in browser DevTools, choose "Copy as cURL", and you get a complete command: URL, headers, body, cookies — everything. The next step is usually reproducing that request in Python: scrapers, API clients, automation checks. The mapping itself is mechanical, but with many flags it's easy to miss one — drop an -H and you get a 401; drop --data-raw and the method silently becomes GET. Mechanical translation is exactly what tools are for: the curl command converter on iLoveDevTool takes the pasted command, generates requests code instantly when you pick the Python target, and can send it straight into an online Python runner to execute.
articles.author: leftzzzz

articles.title: Laravel Excel Exports: The BaseExport Pattern (Reusable)
articles.excerpt: Series: Every Laravel Project Should Have These Building Blocks Part: 22 of 35 Level: Intermediate Prerequisites: Jobs and Queues The BaseExport abstract class pattern Collection exports for small dat…
articles.body: Series: Every Laravel Project Should Have These Building Blocks Part: 22 of 35 Level: Intermediate Prerequisites: Jobs and Queues What You’ll Learn The BaseExport abstract class pattern Collection exports for small datasets Query exports for medium datasets Queueable exports for large datasets Adding formatting, column widths, and headings The Problem: Duplicated Export Code Without a shared base class, every export class reinvents the same boilerplate: heading styles, column widths, date formatting, default heading row setup. Five export classes means five copies of the same configuration. The BaseExport pattern extracts all of that into one place. Each concrete export provides only what’s different: the headers, the data source, and optionally the formatting.
articles.author: Shakil Alam

articles.title: Gravity Forge — a browser game in one folder
articles.excerpt: Small, self-contained browser game: You don't move objects — you bend space Star cores fall from the sky and you never touch them — you bend the space around them. Place gravity nodes that curve the f…
articles.body: Small, self-contained browser game: You don't move objects — you bend space Star cores fall from the sky and you never touch them — you bend the space around them. Place gravity nodes that curve the fall and steer every core into the harvester below. Each wave climbs higher: cores get heavier, wells shift, and the field turns meaner. The stardust you pull in funds the forge, where it buys run upgrades and permanent contracts that give the session a goal. There is a daily We wrote it as a single canvas codebase with no engine and no build step worth mentioning, and it ships through the Playgama Bridge SDK to a dozen portals — the same zip, the rules of each portal handled by a thin layer.

articles.title: CSRF in 2026: SameSite, Fetch Metadata & Origin Checks
articles.excerpt: Earlier this year I reviewed a Node admin panel whose team told me, confidently, that CSRF was "solved by SameSite". They were half right. Their session cookie was SameSite=Lax, which blocks most cros…
articles.body: Earlier this year I reviewed a Node admin panel whose team told me, confidently, that CSRF was "solved by SameSite". They were half right. Their session cookie was SameSite=Lax , which blocks most cross-site form posts. But their "export users" action was a GET route, their marketing site on a sibling subdomain could make same-site requests, and one internal tool set its own cookie with no SameSite attribute at all, which Firefox and Safari do not default to Lax. None of that was exotic. It was three ordinary gaps that SameSite alone could not close. I wrote this with help from AI tools and checked every snippet and config myself against current OWASP CSRF Prevention guidance, Express 5 and Laravel 11.
articles.author: Muhammad Ali Mughal

articles.title: What's inside an .osk file? Packaging an osu! skin correctly
articles.excerpt: An .osk file is how osu! skins are shared. If you write tools around skins, or just want to send your edited skin to a friend, it helps to know exactly what the game expects. An .osk is a normal ZIP a…
articles.body: An .osk file is how osu! skins are shared. If you write tools around skins, or just want to send your edited skin to a friend, it helps to know exactly what the game expects. It's just a zip An .osk is a normal ZIP archive with a different extension. You can open it with any archive tool, and you can create one by zipping a folder and renaming .zip to .osk . cd "My Skin" zip -r "../My Skin.osk" . The one rule people break: no nested folder The files must be at the root of the archive: My Skin.osk ├── skin.ini ├── hitcircle.png ├── hitcircle@2x.png ├── cursor.png └── ... If you zip the folder instead of its contents you get My Skin.osk/My Skin/skin.ini . Depending on the client this imports as an empty skin or the default skin with a strange name. Zip from inside the folder.

articles.excerpt: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space, Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize.
articles.body: On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized.

articles.body: SpaceX has an idea why its latest Starship megarocket test flight missed the first of two planned landings on Friday (Nov. 13), triggering an automatic abort that destroyed the booster. The giant Starship rocket , a massive two-stage vehicle that's the largest launcher on Earth, soared into orbit from SpaceX's Starbase in South Texas on Friday on the company's ambitious Flight 15 test flight. The goal: To land both the Super Heavy first stage and the Ship upper stage, for the first full Starship recovery — and the first complete recovery of an orbital launch system in history. The Super Heavy stage, called Booster 22, came back to Earth mere minutes after liftoff as planned.

articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 astronauts launched to the moon. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier.
articles.author: Hanneke Weitering

articles.body: SpaceX plans to catch the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), and you can watch the action live. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen, however; SpaceX diverted Starship's Super Heavy booster to a controlled splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico 6.5 minutes after launch. Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth .

articles.body: STARBASE, Texas — SpaceX launched the 15th test flight of its massive Starship rocket today (Nov. 13) and is preparing the vehicle's upper stage for its first-ever return to the launch site in less than 24 hours. Flight 15 lifted off from SpaceX 's Starbase facility here in South Texas at 5:47 p.m. ET (2247 GMT; 4:47 p.m. local Texas time). The towering Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage cleared the tower without incident and climbed into the skies under more than 18 million pounds of thrust from the booster's 33 Raptor 3 engines. The flight continued nominally through its initial ascent, with the successful execution of Super Heavy's main engine cutoff and Ship's subsequent hot-staging — firing its own Raptors during separation from the booster — about 2.5 minutes after launch.

articles.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
articles.excerpt: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.
articles.body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions.
